subject: Runtime provider roster snapshot and custody mapping — SIG follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@novamed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Runtime provider roster snapshot and custody mapping — SIG follow-up

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Novamed is finishing our SIG/CAIQ intake for the contract team and we need a compact snapshot of the runtime third‑party roster and custody model for the components that touch live customer tokens (KV cache, ephemeral auth, telemetry collectors). Specifically we need:

- A roster CSV of runtime subproc vendors, with service role (e.g., KV cache, telemetry, queuing), residency (region), and whether they have direct key access.
- A short statement on who controls KMS keys for each provider (Novamed-facing KMS, provider-managed, or Redwood-managed customer keys).
- How on-call access is provisioned for vendor engineers (SSO + JIT, honor-based SSH, VPN, other).
- Any existing SOC 2 / CAIQ crosswalk you can share or a short timeline when we can expect one.

Can you provide the snapshot and an estimated delivery by EOD Monday (your timezone)? Procurement will also need a signed attestation for the KV cache handling. If attachments are large we can accept a secure Drive link.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Security Programs Manager
Novamed Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime provider roster snapshot and custody mapping — SIG follow-up

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is an initial export (redwood-runtime-subprocessor-roster.csv) that maps current runtime providers and primary roles. I also included a short provenance summary (kv_cache_provenance_summary.pdf) that answers the KMS/control question at a high level. Quick notes up front:

- KV cache: primary provider is CacheWave Inc. Keys are customer‑controlled in KMS (we support customer KMS integration; CacheWave never has persistent key access).
- Telemetry collectors: hosted by Redwood, data plane scrubbed prior to export; telemetry vendor partners have scoped access via our telemetry ingest API (no direct DB access).
- On‑call access: vendor engineers use SSO + short‑lived bastion sessions (JIT SSH), audited by our central audit service.

We will prepare a CAIQ/SIG-lite crosswalk and a signed attestation for the KV cache handling. Karthik will run the KMS/key custody paragraphs past legal for any redaction needs. For larger bundles I can upload to a secure Drive link — see the draft link below.

Deliverables planned:
- CSV roster (attached) — immediate
- SIG-lite evidence index (sig-lite-evidence-index.xlsx) — by end of day Monday 2026-08-16
- Signed KV cache attestation (DocuSign) — by 2026-08-17

Let me know if you prefer the Drive upload or a HubSpot/Portal upload.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@novamed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>, Novamed Security Team <security@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime provider roster snapshot and custody mapping — SIG follow-up

Marissa —

Received the CSV and the provenance summary, thanks. A couple quick clarifications before we finalize:

1) For CacheWave Inc — can you confirm whether any replication or failover keys are stored outside the primary KMS region? Novamed requires confirmation that keys do not transit outside the contracted residency.
2) For on‑call access: does Redwood issue the short‑lived bastion tokens (i.e., Redwood‑controlled JIT) or are they issued by the vendor and logged into Redwood? We want to be sure vendor engineers cannot persist credentials.

Procurement asked if you can sign a short attestation covering the above two points and whether your SOC 2 scope includes the KV cache and telemetry pipeline. I started a DocuSign envelope (link below) to make signature easier. If needed we can accept a portal upload instead.

DocuSign (proposed attestation): https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123DEF

Thanks,
Jordan
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@novamed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime provider roster snapshot and custody mapping — SIG follow-up

Jordan — quick summary to close the loop: answers below and I've attached the SIG-lite index for reference.

- KV cache (CacheWave Inc): No replication keys are stored outside the customer‑designated KMS region. We use customer‑managed keys; CacheWave only receives ephemeral, encrypted session tokens when required for specific maintenance tasks.
- On‑call access: Redwood issues short‑lived bastion sessions through our SSO/JIT platform and logs all session activity into our audit ledger. Vendor engineers do not receive persistent credentials.
- SOC 2 scope: KV cache and the telemetry ingest pipeline are in our scope for infrastructure and availability controls; we can provide the SOC 2 mapping page via secure link upon request.

Attached: sig-lite-evidence-index.xlsx (index of artifacts we will share). We will complete the DocuSign attestation today and upload the final bundle to the secure Drive link below. Proposed next steps:
1) We sign and return the attestation (DocuSign).
2) We upload the full SIG-lite artifact pack to the Drive link for Novamed security review.
3) If Novamed needs a formal residency addendum, legal can follow with a one‑paragraph rider.

Drive upload (incoming): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1ABcDexample

Ben Carter
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
